inspiration: Layered damage fallback: a primary formula, then a weaker attack-only fallback, then zero, then small bonus terms. Keep the layered fallback so a hit never reads as zero without reason; use our own numbers in data.
Chip strike when out of resource: a caster without the resource still does a small random hit. Keep the no-dead-air hit; show a strained state instead of a free damage number.
Cover shapes as data: point, line, cross, rectangle, rhombus and area, with a distance rule per shape. Keep the taxonomy and the distance rule; ours are arc and cone in 3D with a ground telegraph.
Scored cast chooser: a score per candidate cast and target, summed over the shape, best score wins. Keep the score-per-shape idea and add threat and leash terms.

Designer sheet grammar: a marker cell, a description row, a type row, a name row, then data rows with list separators. Keep designer-edited sheets with type checks; ours is a validated JSON or CSV catalogue.
Resistance-then-clamp status effects: skill minus resistance, integer, clamped at zero. Keep the clamp-at-zero rule for poison-like effects.
Battle logic split by responsibility: init, manager, AI, range and damage in separate modules. Keep the split; ours stays one engine in src/fight.
